To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

brain extracts from 8 day old chick embryos have stimulatory effects on size of somas and on the growth of long processes of dissociated brain neurons from 7-day chick embryos in culture, and that these effects are parallel to modifications of various enzyme activity according to the age in the cultures.

the addition of brain extract from 8-day old chick embryos to 7-day-old brain cells in culture results in a stimulation of adenyl cyclase, 5'-nucleotidases, choline acetytransferase, and Mg2+ and (Na+, K+) ATPases, and an increase in acetylcholinestrase activity.

brain extracts of 8-day-old chicks stimulated the growth of nerve cells in culture from 7-day embryos, and that this growth was accompanied by modifications of some enzyme activities, such as adenyl cyclase, ATPase, 5’-nucleotides, choline acetytransferase, and total acetylcholine esterase.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the effects of embryo brain extracts on the development of chick embryo brain nerve cell cultures.
the influence of brain extracts on the development in culture of chick embryo brain cells and with the parallel modifications of some enzyme activities.
the study of a factor present in chick embryo brain extract that is able to stimulate nerve cell development.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
brain extracts contain factors which are capable of stimulating morphological development of brain nerve cell culture, which is paralleled by biochemical changes in the cells.

these results are in favor of the existence of a factor or factors present in the cytosol and/or dialysate of chick embryo brain extracts which are able to influence the development of chick brain nerve cells in vitro.
the extracts of 8-day-old embryo brain are able to modify the development of nerve cells of 7-day-old embryos in culture, and this effect is correlated with modifications of some enzyme activities.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the brain extracts from chick embryo brain are capable of inducing biochemical and morphological changes in the nerve cells of chick embryo brain in culture.
brain extracts are able to modify enzyme activities and thus to influence morphological differentiation of chick embryo brain cells in culture.
the brain extracts contain a factor that can influence morphological and biochemical development of chick embryo brain cells.
The main takeaway from our work is that
chick embryo extracts are a good tool for studying the development of neuronal cells in culture.
chick embryo brain extracts can influence the biochemical development of cultured chick embryo brain cells.
the biochemical modifications observed in nerve cells treated by brain extract are similar to the modifications observed during embryogenesis.
